subject: Re: Northwind escalation — tail latency bursts follow-up + benchmark rerun after KV compaction rollout (SUP-28411)
body:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Northwind escalation — tail latency bursts follow-up + benchmark rerun after KV compaction rollout (SUP-28411)

Sean — looping you in. Northwind is asking to re-run the exact burst scenario that triggered SUP-28411 now that the compaction canary is expanded.

Can you confirm:
1) whether compaction is enabled for their cohort in us-west-2 hosted,
2) what guardrails we want to use as “pass/fail” (p99, eviction rate, compaction bytes moved),
3) what we can safely share externally (high-level results vs screenshots).

Also, can we propose a 30-min review early next week? They’re pushing for an exec-ready update.

- Nikhil

---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Northwind escalation — tail latency bursts follow-up + benchmark rerun after KV compaction rollout (SUP-28411)

Yep.

1) They’re currently on hosted pool “hapi-usw2-a”, which as of Thu night has compaction ON for ~25% traffic via the runtime-1.22 canary. Northwind org is in the canary allowlist (added during SUP-28411 mitigation).

2) Guardrails I’d use for the rerun (same as our rollout gates):
- p99 decode latency: must not regress >10% vs their Jan 28 baseline
- p95 overall request latency: must improve or hold flat
- eviction events: should be near-zero during the run; if non-zero, we need to call it out explicitly and explain why it’s safe
- compaction work: keep under budget (we track it internally as time + bytes moved; I’ll summarize as “background memory housekeeping” externally)

3) External sharing: we can share aggregated before/after numbers and a short narrative. No internal dashboard screenshots.

I can join a 30-min review Tue/Wed.

Sean

---

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 10:28 AM PST
Subject: Re: Northwind escalation — tail latency bursts follow-up + benchmark rerun after KV compaction rollout (SUP-28411)

+1.

Let’s be precise in language:
- We’re not “defragmenting live allocations” in a way that changes outputs; it’s memory layout management in the KV arena.
- The only customer-visible effect should be fewer tail spikes under churn/bursts.

Nikhil — suggest we propose: rerun the same load shape + the same prompt-length distribution for 45 minutes (to allow fragmentation to build) and compare:
- baseline (compaction disabled cohort) vs canary cohort.

If they need a single number: use p99 and number of >X sec outliers.

Mateo

---

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Park <evelyn.park@northwindanalytics.com>
Cc: Jordan Kim <jordan.kim@northwindanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 11:11 AM PST
Subject: Re: Northwind escalation — tail latency bursts follow-up + benchmark rerun plan (SUP-28411)

Evelyn — thanks again for the detailed traces on SUP-28411.

We’ve rolled out an improvement on our hosted runtime targeted specifically at KV-cache memory fragmentation (a known driver of burst-driven tail spikes under mixed sequence lengths). Your org is included in the current canary cohort in us-west.

Proposal for a clean verification rerun:
- Run duration: 45 minutes (we want enough time for fragmentation pressure to build)
- Workload: same burst pattern + the same prompt/response length mix as the Jan 28 run
- Outputs: we’ll report back with before/after summary (p95/p99 + count of extreme outliers)

Two quick asks so we can match the prior run closely:
1) Can you confirm the exact request rate profile you used (ramp + peak + cooldown) and concurrency target?
2) If possible, include one additional header on your side with a test-run ID so we can correlate quickly (e.g., X-Northwind-Run: 2026-02-10-a).

If you’re available, I’d like to set up a 30-min review to walk through results and next steps.
- Tue 2/10 2:00–2:30pm PT or Wed 2/11 10:00–10:30am PT

We’ll keep the update concrete and focused on the tail latency behavior you escalated.

Best,
Nikhil

Nikhil Sharma
Product — Hosted API
Redwood Inference

---

From: Evelyn Park <evelyn.park@northwindanalytics.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Kim <jordan.kim@northwindanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 9, 2026 at 8:36 AM PST
Subject: Re: Northwind escalation — tail latency bursts follow-up + benchmark rerun plan (SUP-28411)

Thanks Nikhil.

We can rerun tomorrow (Tue). 2:00pm PT works.

Re: run details — the Jan 28 profile was:
- 10 min warmup at 40 rps
- 15 min steady at 80 rps
- 5 min burst to 160 rps (we do 3 bursts, 60s each, with 90s at 80 rps between)
- 15 min cooldown at 60 rps

Concurrency cap was 600 in our loadgen.

We can add the header you mentioned.

One more request: if you can share any guidance on what we should monitor in our app logs during the test (e.g., retries/timeouts), that would help.

Evelyn

---

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Park <evelyn.park@northwindanalytics.com>
Cc: Jordan Kim <jordan.kim@northwindanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 9, 2026 at 9:22 AM PST
Subject: Re: Northwind escalation — tail latency bursts follow-up + benchmark rerun plan (SUP-28411)

Perfect — thanks for the exact profile.

For your app-side monitoring during the rerun, we suggest tracking:
- client-side timeouts (count + max)
- retry rate (if you have automatic retries enabled)
- HTTP 429/503 counts (should remain near zero; if not, we want to know immediately)
- request latency distribution on your side (p95/p99)

If you can capture a small sample of the slowest-request IDs/timestamps (top ~20) that’s usually enough for us to correlate with our traces.

Attached is a short one-pager of the rerun plan + what we’ll report back.

Attachment: Northwind_benchmark_rerun_plan_v1.pdf

See you Tue at 2:00pm PT. I’ll send a calendar hold separately.

Best,
Nikhil

---

From: Jordan Kim <jordan.kim@northwindanalytics.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evelyn Park <evelyn.park@northwindanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 4:42 PM PST
Subject: Re: Northwind escalation — tail latency bursts follow-up + benchmark rerun plan (SUP-28411)

Thanks — rerun completed.

We tagged requests with:
X-Northwind-Run: 2026-02-10-a

No 429s/503s. Retries were near zero (we saw 11 total across the full run). We did still see a small number of >6s outliers during the third burst, but it looked materially better than the Jan 28 run.

We’ll come to the review with our percentile charts.

Jordan

(also attaching the fields we captured per request)

Attachment: northwind_trace_request_fields.txt
